articles.title: Independence Day Festival:Priyank Kharge Directs Police ,GBA to Strengthen Security and ...
articles.content: Pramesh S Jain Karnataka Home Minister,Priyank Kharge on Wednesday directed senior police and Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) officials to make comprehensive security and traffic arrangements for the state’s first public ‘Independence Festival–2026’,scheduled to be held at the historic Vidhana Soudha on August 15. Kharge chaired a meeting with senior officials to review security,traffic management,public entry and exit, parking and crowd-control arrangements ahead of the event,which is expected to draw large crowds. The festival will be held from 11 am to 10 pm and will feature the ‘The People’s India Parade’,a special tour of Vidhana Soudha,a children’s fair,quiz competitions, cultural programmes,a music concert and food and handicraft exhibitions showcasing various districts of Karnataka. With a large turnout expected for the evening music programme and fireworks display,Kharge instructed officials to make special arrangements for crowd management and public safety. He directed the authorities to ensure smooth traffic flow, pedestrian safety,emergency-response arrangements and adequate crowd-control measures so that visitors do not face inconvenience. Kharge also stressed the need for close coordination among the police,GBA and other departments to ensure that there are no lapses in public safety during the celebrations. GBA Chief Commissioner,M.Maheshwar Rao,Bengaluru City Police Commissioner,Seemant Kumar Singh,and senior officials from the police,GBA and other concerned departments attended the meeting.

articles.title: Kuku TV Launches India's First Acting Reality Microdrama, Sabse Bada Dramebaaz
articles.content: Technology For SMEs Kuku TV Launches India’s First Acting Reality Microdrama, Sabse Bada Dramebaaz Kuku TV launches Sabse Bada Dramebaaz, India’s first acting reality microdrama, featuring 12 finalists competing for ₹5 lakh and lead roles. SMEStreet Edit Desk 13 Aug 2026 11:50 IST Follow Us New Update Listen to this article 0.75x 1x 1.5x 00:00 / 00:00 Kuku TV, India’s leading premium microdrama app, has launched Sabse Bada Dramebaaz, India’s first acting reality microdrama, co-presented with Meesho and powered by Tinder. The 50-episode series brings the reality-show format to vertical, mobile-first entertainment, with episodes of approximately two minutes each. The nationwide talent hunt received over 2,000 audition entries, generating crores of views and lakhs of audience votes. The 100 most-voted entries advanced to the next stage, from which 11 finalists were selected by Kuku TV’s microdrama actors Eshaanya Maheshwari and Siddharth Sharma. The 12th finalist earned a wildcard entry through the Meesho Creator Club. The competition then moved to Mumbai, where the Top 12 contestants competed across four offline rounds in front of a live audience and a judging panel comprising veteran actor Rakesh Bedi and actors and digital personalities Jannat Zubair and Prince Narula. The trio’s association with Sabse Bada Dramebaaz marks their first association with a microdrama, with Prince and Jannat also performing in the show. The show brings together romance, action, comedy, suspense and drama within a reality competition format, combining talent discovery with Kuku TV’s microdrama storytelling model. The first three rounds, spanning nearly 30 episodes, are streaming on the Kuku TV app, with the Grand Finale releasing on 15th August’26. At the end of the competition, two winners, one male and one female, will each receive a cash prize of ₹5 lakh and the opportunity to play lead roles in upcoming Kuku TV microdramas. Commenting on the launch, Sachin Singh, Head of Kuku TV, said, "At Kuku TV, creator empowerment, content innovation, and audience entertainment are at the heart of what we do. We have built an ecosystem that empowers more than 50,000 creators, while continuing to take bold bets on new content experiences for microdrama, informed by our understanding of audiences and powered by our AI storytelling stack. Sabse Bada Dramebaaz brings these strengths together. We are also excited to bring Meesho and Tinder, two of India’s leading new-age brands, together for this first-of-its-kind format.” Speaking about the partnership, Nikita Dawda, General Manager, Content Commerce, Meesho, said, "Creators today are shaping how millions of people discover products, ideas and culture, making the creator economy one of the most exciting shifts shaping India. At Meesho, we’ve seen this first-hand through our community of over 5 lakh creators across Bharat, where the Meesho Creator Club is helping creators access the right opportunities to grow and reach new audiences. We’re excited to partner with Kuku TV to nurture the next generation of creators and aspiring actors through this initiative, giving them a platform to showcase their talent and take the next step in their creative journey. articles.title: Prakriti Gyan Dham: India's First Eco-Educational Hub - INSIGHTS IAS
articles.content: Source: TOI Subject: Government Scheme Context: Union Minister of State for Science and Technology dedicated Prakriti Gyan Dham , India’s first-of-its-kind eco-educational hub, to the nation. The Eco-Educational Hub About The Eco-Educational Hub : What It Is? Prakriti Gyan Dham (The Eco-Educational Hub) is an interactive, open-air eco-educational facility and living repository of India’s rich botanical wealth, heritage trees, and environmental research. It serves as a walkable classroom designed for students, researchers, nature enthusiasts, and farmers to engage directly with plant science and sustainable bio-resources . Location: Maharishi Parashar Bioresource Centre (MPBC) in Banthra, on the outskirts of Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh. Developing Agency: CSIR-National Botanical Research Institute (CSIR-NBRI), Lucknow. Aim: To extend scientific research beyond institutional laboratory walls into society, fostering experiential environmental education, preserving botanical-cultural heritage , promoting threatened plant conservation, and driving livelihood generation through bio-technologies. Key Features: PAaVan Path (Heritage Trail): The centerpiece of the hub—Plants and Associated Vegetations for Appreciating Nature—is an interpretive trail displaying curated plant species representing India’s diverse ecological regions. Indian Heritage Garden with Interactive QR Systems : Features cloned descendants of historically sacred and freedom-struggle trees paired with smartphone-scannable QR audio-guides. The Bamboosteum: Houses 43 indigenous and exotic bamboo species demonstrating their role as carbon-sequestering, renewable bioresources for soil restoration, green infrastructure, and sustainable rural crafts. Conservation Enclaves (Vibhav & Bhairav): Vibhav Enclave: Dedicated to preserving India’s rare, endangered, and threatened (RET) plant species. Bhairav Enclave: Features a living map of the official State Plants of all Indian States and Union Territories . Lab-to-Society Technology Transfer: Integrates practical bio-technology commercialization on-site, including the official launch and tech-transfer of herbal health formulations developed with industrial partners. Significance: Pioneers a Lab-to-Land model that translates complex botanical and ecological research into an accessible public format, raising environmental literacy across communities. Preserves historically significant living trees alongside endangered native flora and eco-tourism across CSIR institutions

articles.title: Island Computing to launch India's first fully managed sovereign cloud platform on August 15
articles.content: Industry 2 min read Island Computing to launch India's first fully managed sovereign cloud platform on August 15 The company said the platform will offer 30% lower costs than equivalent AWS Mumbai configurations on its published benchmark workload and keep data, infrastructure and cloud operations within India. ETEnterpriseAI Desk ETEnterpriseAI Published On Aug 12, 2026 at 06:36 PM IST Select ETEnterpriseAI as Preferred Choice on Google Copy Link Share on WhatsApp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook The platform has been designed and built in India, with its data centres, hardware infrastructure, operating entity, cloud operations, identity systems and audit logs remaining within India and aligned with Indian law. Bengaluru-based cloud infrastructure company Island Computing on Wednesday said it will launch its fully managed sovereign cloud platform in India on August 15, targeting startups, AI and SaaS companies, banks, government bodies and other enterprises with workloads requiring greater jurisdictional control. The company said the platform has been designed and built in India, with its data centres, hardware infrastructure, operating entity, cloud operations, identity systems and audit logs remaining within India and aligned with Indian law. Advt The platform will support modern workloads including multi-tenant SaaS, long-running agentic execution and regulated artificial intelligence (AI) applications using Indian data, the company said. The company added its published benchmark showed the platform costs 30 per cent less than equivalent configurations on the AWS Mumbai region, before committed-use or enterprise discounts. Cloud platform The platform uses a distributed control and data plane designed to remain fault-tolerant across data centres. It also uses a microVM-based hypervisor for tenant isolation, while network topology, autoscaling, observability and identity are configured by the platform. The company said customers can provision an "Island" in 90 seconds and deploy a production-grade application in three minutes. The platform is designed to abstract infrastructure complexity and reduce DevOps requirements for customers. The platform is designed around requirements under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, Reserve Bank of India data-localisation circulars, Securities and Exchange Board of India cloud advisories and CERT-In's incident-reporting directive, the company said. Target sectors The platform will be generally available from August 15 to enterprises, government bodies and developers across India. Partner onboarding will also begin on the same day for businesses working across BFSI, healthcare, telecommunications, public sector, IoT, SaaS, video, gaming and agentic AI. Advt "Sovereignty isn't a constraint, it's a competitive advantage. It means our banks, our government, and our builders can move fast without ever giving up control of the stack their future runs on," said Vishal Sirohi, Founder and CEO, Island Computing. articles.title: PayU launches India's first RBI-compliant accessible payments - VARIndia.
articles.content: HOME Breaking News PayU launches India’s first RBI-compliant accessible payments checkout for visually impaired users How does PayUs new accessible payments checkout cater to the needs of visually impaired users in India? What specific features have been implemented to ensure compliance with RBI guidelines for accessibility in PayUs new payment checkout? How will the introduction of this new accessible payment option impact the overall payment experience for visually impaired users in India? by VARINDIA 2026-08-12 The new payment solution introduces screen-reader support, adaptive interfaces and visual accessibility features, enabling users with blindness, low vision and other accessibility needs to complete digital transactions more independently and confidently. PayU has introduced an accessibility-focused payment checkout platform designed for people who are blind or visually impaired, becoming the first payment gateway in India to align with the Reserve Bank of India’s accessibility requirements announced in October 2024. The new Accessible Payments Checkout is aimed at making digital transactions easier for users with visual and cognitive accessibility needs by improving navigation, discoverability and interaction during the payment process. The launch comes as India continues to expand digital payment adoption and strengthen financial inclusion initiatives. The solution is compliant with the RBI’s BIS IS 17802 accessibility standards and reflects a growing focus within the fintech sector on ensuring that digital services can be used independently by all sections of society. Features designed for inclusive payments PayU’s accessibility-focused checkout integrates several features intended to support users with different accessibility requirements. One of the key additions is full screen-reader optimisation, enabling users to navigate the payment journey through voice prompts and audio feedback. Payment options such as UPI, net banking, QR code payments and NEFT can be accessed without requiring sighted assistance, while transaction details and payment stages are announced clearly. The platform also includes adaptive user profiles, allowing users to customise interface elements such as cursor size, button dimensions and navigation settings. Preferences can be saved and adjusted according to individual requirements. To support users with low vision, colour blindness or light sensitivity, the checkout offers visual inclusivity modes, including high-contrast settings, greyscale mode, colour inversion and saturation adjustments. Text resizing of up to 200% is also supported without affecting the layout or readability of content. "True financial inclusion is only possible when every individual can access and use digital payments independently. At PayU, accessibility is not an afterthought - it's a core design principle. With the launch of our Accessibility Checkout, we're helping merchants deliver payment experiences that are inclusive by design while enabling millions of users with diverse accessibility needs to participate more confidently in India's digital economy. This is an important step towards supporting the RBI's accessibility vision and building digital infrastructure that works for everyone," said Manas Mishra, Chief Product Officer, PayU and Wibmo . Accessibility without additional merchant integration PayU said merchants using its payment gateway will not need to modify their existing integrations to offer the new accessibility features. articles.title: PayU Launches India's First RBI-Compliant Accessible Payments Checkout for Blind and ...
articles.content: PayU today announced the launch of Accessible Payments Checkout, India’s first RBI-compliant payment checkout designed for people who are blind or visually impaired. The launch marks a significant step towards making digital payments more accessible and inclusive. As the country celebrates Independence Day, the launch reinforces the importance of ensuring that everyone can participate in the digital economy with greater independence. With this launch, PayU becomes the first payment gateway in India to comply with the Reserve Bank of India’s October 2024 accessibility mandate (BIS IS 17802). The enhanced checkout introduces a range of features designed to improve discoverability, navigation, and interaction for users with visual and cognitive accessibility needs, making the online payment journey more seamless and intuitive. The solution reflects PayU’s continued commitment to building inclusive financial technology and enabling every user to access digital payments with confidence and ease. The new PayU Accessibility Checkout includes four key features: Full-Screen-Reader Optimisation: PayU’s Accessibility Checkout is engineered to work seamlessly with screen readers, ensuring easy navigation of the entire payment journey for the visually impaired and blind without any sighted assistance. From choosing the payment method like Net banking, UPI, QR, NEFT, etc. to payment amount confirmation and transaction completion, every element on the checkout page is clearly and transparently announced via voice commands to the user, ensuring they know where exactly they are in their payment journey. Adaptive User Profiles: This feature allows users to customize their checkout environments – adjusting cursor size, button dimensions, and navigation aids to fit their requirements. Their preferences can be saved, switched between or reset at any point. The checkout adapts as the user wants, delivering complete control in the hands of the user. Visual Inclusivity Modes: To aid users with conditions such as low vision, colour blindness, or light sensitivity, a wide variety of visual modes are offered by PayU’s Accessibility Checkout. From high contrast to greyscale mode to colour inversion to saturation adjustment options, the checkout offers support to the visually impaired users who rely on colour and contrast adaptations to use digital platforms. Text Resizing: The Accessibility Checkout supports text scaling of up to 200% of the standard size, without overlapping or hiding any content. This feature ensures all elements on the checkout is transparently seen and read by the users with visual impairments. “True financial inclusion is only possible when every individual can access and use digital payments independently. At PayU, accessibility is not an afterthought – it’s a core design principle. With the launch of our Accessibility Checkout, we’re helping merchants deliver payment experiences that are inclusive by design while enabling millions of users with diverse accessibility needs to participate more confidently in India’s digital economy. This is an important step towards supporting the RBI’s accessibility vision and building digital infrastructure that works for everyone,” said Manas Mishra, Chief Product Officer, PayU and Wibmo. articles.title: Keralite engineers behind India's first private orbital rocket meet Kerala CM
articles.content: THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: A team of Keralite engineers who played a key role in developing Vikram-1, India’s first privately developed orbital rocket, called on Chief Minister V D Satheesan on Tuesday. Seven of the 14-member team at Hyderabad-based Skyroot Aerospace visited Satheesan at his office. The team included Nirmal Nelson, who coordinated the launch vehicle’s electro-mechanical systems, Ajith Kumar S, who was part of the liquid propulsion stage design, Dr Binet Monachan, who handled design and testing of the fluid control system, Ajin Ghosh K, K and Ranjith Ravi, who contributed to propulsion system design, Lint C Thomas and Anjali Ashokan, members of the avionics quality and reliability team. Vaisakh V, Ramshij M, Anantha Krishnan, Vishnu M K, Sreenath S, Rahul Ramesh and Alexis J Neerakkal are the other members working at Skyroot. The chief minister said the significant contribution of Malayalis behind the historic achievement was a matter of pride for the state. articles.title: India's Gen Z and the AI Era: Turning Demographic Strength into an AI Dividend
articles.content: August 11, 2026 Gen Z: India’s first AI generation Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Rajesh Seth Gen Z holds the key to transforming India’s demographic dividend into a lasting AI dividend ‘Gen Z’ has emerged as one of the most talked — about terms in India in recent past. The spotlight on this generation reflects a growing recognition that its aspirations, choices and capabilities will profoundly influence the country’s future. Yet an even bigger story is unfolding beyond the headlines. Gen Z is India’s first generation to step into higher education and the workplace in the age of AI. For the Baby Boomers, the defining technology was television. Generation X witnessed the rise of the personal computer. Millennials transformed the smartphone into an indispensable companion. Gen Z grew up in the age of social media, with platforms such as Instagram becoming integral to communication, creativity and self-expression. It is now the first generation to begin its professional journey alongside AI. Unlike earlier technological revolutions that unfolded over decades, AI is evolving at a remarkable speed. India’s AI dividend India is uniquely placed in this transformation. With one of the world’s youngest populations, the country possesses an extraordinary demographic advantage. Yet demographics alone do not guarantee prosperity. India’s demographic dividend will remain a statistic unless it is transformed into an economic and an AI dividend. That transformation will depend on whether its Gen Z are equipped to thrive in an AI-driven world. India’s digital public infrastructure, expanding startup ecosystem and growing adoption of AI across sectors provide fertile ground for innovation. If educational institutions, industry and policymakers work in concert, the country has an opportunity not merely to participate in the global AI revolution, but to help shape it. AI is already changing the nature of work. Routine tasks such as drafting documents, analysing large volumes of data, scheduling activities and generating basic content are increasingly being automated. Consequently, employers are beginning to value qualities that machines cannot easily replicate, like critical thinking, creativity, ethical judgement, learning agility and emotional intelligence. AI is not simply changing jobs; it is changing the skills that make people employable. The future belongs to those who can outthink AI. AI as a thinking partner This presents both an opportunity and a challenge for India’s Gen Z. Unlike earlier generations, today’s students have unprecedented access to powerful AI tools that can explain concepts, summarize information, generate ideas and accelerate learning. However, frequent use of AI should not be mistaken for AI literacy. Knowing how to use an AI application is very different from knowing how to frame effective prompts, verify responses, recognise inaccuracies and apply AI thoughtfully. True AI literacy also means understanding AI’s limitations, recognising bias, safeguarding privacy and knowing when human judgement must prevail. AI should become a thinking partner, not a thinking substitute. Across classrooms and campuses, one sees students increasingly turning to AI for explanations, summaries and assignments. This need not be viewed with alarm. Every transformative technology has altered the...

articles.title: Mercedes-Benz Launches AI Vehicle Scanner And Service Select | Autocar Professional
articles.content: Mercedes-Benz has introduced an AI-powered vehicle scanner, Service Select for older cars and a new Mumbai facility as part of its service network expansion. 12 Aug 2026 | 18 Views | By Eshisha Java Mercedes-Benz India has introduced an AI-powered automated Vehicle Scanner, launched the Service Select programme for cars aged seven years and inaugurated a new service facility in Mumbai. The initiatives are part of the company’s efforts to expand its service offerings and reduce ownership costs. The Vehicle Scanner, deployed at the Landmark Cars service facility in Jogeshwari, Mumbai, is described by Mercedes-Benz as India’s first AI-powered automated vehicle scanner deployed by an automaker. It uses a 360-degree high-resolution camera system to digitally record the vehicle’s exterior condition, identify damage and assess tyre tread depth. Mercedes-Benz India Managing Director and CEO Santosh Iyer said, “Introduction of India’s first AI-driven, automated vehicle scanner marks an important step in the deployment of AI and automation for driving transparency, trust and efficiency.” Service Select has been introduced as a customer loyalty programme for Mercedes-Benz vehicles that are seven years old. The programme offers savings of up to 25 per cent on select parts, Mobilio Lite benefits, a two-year warranty on parts and expert care aimed at protecting residual value. The company also lists its STAR EASE Service Package, three-year standard warranty and extended warranty of up to six years among its ownership-cost offerings. Mercedes-Benz says its service network comprises more than 90 service touchpoints and 1,200 service bays, supported by more than 4,200 employees. Other service initiatives include MB. CHARGE Public, the MBFS Mobile App and the India-developed SKYLine dealer management system. Mercedes-Benz also offers Premier Express Prime, Fast Lane B&P and Doorstep Mobile Service, along with services such as HV Battery Reports, Collision Care Connected Support and mobility assistance with tele-diagnostics and live tracking. The Vehicle Scanner captures the vehicle’s complete exterior condition as it passes through the system. The images are automatically anonymised, while AI identifies external damage and measures tyre tread depth. The information is then added to the workshop order and reception report, linking the scan to the service job without manual entry. The system provides service advisors with real-time vehicle data on tablets and allows customers to view a digital record of the vehicle’s condition before approving required work. Mercedes-Benz says automated documentation is intended to reduce paperwork and waiting times during service reception. The new Landmark Cars facility is Mercedes-Benz’s 14th luxury facility in Mumbai and the city’s largest luxury service facility, according to the company. Spread across approximately 58,000 sq ft, it has 16 preventive maintenance and general repair bays, nine body and paint bays and nine supporting bays, along with a 6,000 sq ft spare-parts area. The facility has approximately 95 trained professionals. Mercedes-Benz India plans to add more than 20 luxury outlets during 2026, with more than ₹450 crore in investment committed by franchise partners over the next two years.
